item.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_2^7$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a nonempty subset of the binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ is spectral if and only if it tiles $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ by translations. This is the smallest binary dimension left open by Ferguson and Sothanaphan. For the implication from tiling to spectrality we show that every eight-point subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ admits $2^{d-3}$ frequencies whose pairwise differences avoid the zeros of its Fourier transform; consequently every tile of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ with at least $2^{d-3}$ elements is spectral. For the converse implication, we use the Smith normal form of the Walsh matrix to exclude every spectral subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^7$, and of $\mathbb{F}_2^8$, whose size is not a power of two. The sizes $16$ and $32$ are reduced, by a projection argument, to the tiling of point sets attached to binary log-Hadamard matrices of small rank. Using the published classifications of Hadamard matrices of orders $16$ and $32$, we find that exactly sixteen order-$32$ classes up to transposition have dephased binary rank at most seven, and we give explicit tilings for both orientations of each.
item.dc:creator: Atsushi Kadowaki

item.title: Time-and-band limiting for symmetric classical Dunkl orthogonal polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.24100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem of ''time and band limiting'' has been previously considered for expansions in orthonormal polynomials that are common eigenfunctions of some second order differential operator. In this paper we consider the situation of orthonormal polynomials that are eigenfunctions of some second order differential-difference operator as introduced by Ch. Dunkl. These polynomials appear already in the work of G. Szeg\H{o} and at the same time play a role in supersymmetric quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: M. M. Castro, F. A. Gr\"unbaum

item.title: end point estimates for the bilinear circular averaging operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.24465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the bilinear circular averaging operator is bounded from $L^1(\mathbb{R}) \times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$. The corresponding strong estimate fails, even when the inputs are nonnegative, smooth, and compactly supported. We also construct nonnegative $f,g \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ for which the average does not belong to $L^{1/2}(\mathbb{R})$. The weak estimate is proved by a dyadic decomposition of the inputs and a summation over interval pairs near each quadratic fold.
item.dc:creator: Xuyi Wei

item.title: Lyapunov-Krasovsky Functionals and the Existence of Unbounded Solutions of Functional-Differential Equations of Retarded Type
item.description: arXiv:2610.24620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, the concepts of unboundedness and partial unboundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type are introduced. On the basis of the method of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, sufficient conditions for the existence of partially unbounded solutions are obtained. As corollaries, sufficient conditions for the existence of unbounded solutions are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Lapin K. S., Lapin S. V

item.title: Asymptotics of Weighted Bergman Polynomials under Finite Regularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.24693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study strong asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials with respect to fixed weighted area measures on Jordan domains. The aim is to understand how the regularity of the domain and the weight enter the large-degree asymptotic behavior of these polynomials. For domains with real-analytic boundaries, Suetin established leading-order asymptotics for H\"older continuous weights, while Hedenmalm--Wennman obtained a full asymptotic expansion for real-analytic weights. We interpolate between these results while allowing both the boundary and the weight to have finite smoothness. The resulting expansions have a length determined by the available regularity and hold in the exterior region and, under sufficient regularity conditions, in a shrinking neighborhood of the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Lennart Aljoscha H\"ubner

item.title: A curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.24850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Lebesgue space estimates for a curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform associated with the moment curve $t \mapsto (t,t^2,t^3)$. The analysis relies on smoothing inequalities for curved multilinear averages and on estimates for a three-dimensional anisotropic variant of the twisted paraproduct. The result has been formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Polona Durcik, Marco Fraccaroli, Joris Roos

item.title: On the frequency function of periodic quasianalytic and non-quasianalytic functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.24953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a real-valued continuous periodic function $f$, let \[ A_r f(x)=\frac{1}{2r}\int_{x-r}^{x+r}f(t)\,dt,\qquad A_0f(x)=f(x), \] and let $r_f(x)$ be the smallest radius at which $\sup_{r\geq 0}A_r f(x)$ is attained. We call $r_f$ the frequency function of $f$. Steinerberger proved that a two-valued condition involving both $r_f$ and $r_{-f}$ characterizes a single sinusoidal function, and asked if the same result holds under the assumption that $r_f$ has finite range (or even range with Lebesgue measure zero). In this paper, we prove that a stronger finite-valued condition for $r_f$ characterizes a sinusoidal function for the case when $f$ is periodic, smooth, and belongs to a quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman class. However, we also show that the conjecture of Steinerberger is not true in general, since we can construct non-sinusoidal periodic smooth functions in non-quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes such that their frequency functions have finite range.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Garz\'on, Jos\'e Madrid

item.title: Advancing the Theory of Sheffer Sequences via Dual Pad\'e Rational Approximants
item.description: arXiv:2610.25457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sheffer sequences offer an operational framework that unifies a wide range of classical polynomial families. In this article, a rational approximation is developed for both the amplitude and the delta-operator symbol in the exponential generating function. The resulting Pad\'e Sheffer polynomials are shown, within the umbral calculus framework, to retain the Sheffer structure. Explicit operational representations are obtained, together with finite-order differential recurrences and closed-form connection constants characterizing the deviation from the underlying polynomial family. An important consequence of the construction is that rational generating indicators reduce the usual transcendental Lagrange inversion problem to a finite multinomial computation. The framework also suggests an interpretation in terms of weighted finite automata, linking polynomial constructions with state-space dynamics for unbounded combinatorial partitions.
item.dc:creator: Ujair Ahmad, Subuhi Khan

item.title: The $(n-2)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb R^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a proof for the $(n-2)$-linear extension estimate for curved surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge5$, at the local product exponent $2(n-1)/(n-2)^2$, with an arbitrarily small power loss. The hypotheses are transversality of the normals and nondegeneracy of the compressed shape operators on their common two-dimensional orthogonal complement. The argument combines polynomial partitioning, a descent through algebraic varieties, localized multilinear restriction, and positive packet-energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Faruk Temur

item.title: Diamond Maximal Operators: Classification, Moduli, and Oscillation Envelopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study maximal averages generated by bounded cancellative kernels taking values in finite-dimensional real normed spaces, on Euclidean balls and on balls in a non-Archimedean local field with a fixed uniformizer. For angular kernels, pointwise domination of the full maximal operators is equivalent to factorization of their angular averaging maps, with the same optimal constant. Nonzero scalar angular comparison classes are therefore projective kernel classes. For angular kernels constant on a fixed finite measurable partition of the direction space, symmetric convex bodies classify exact norm measurements, Grassmannians parametrize nonzero classes under mutual domination, and positive semidefinite Gram matrices classify Hilbert-valued measurements. For general kernels, the closed convex hull of the averaging densities obtained from all scales and the dual unit ball is a complete invariant of the full maximal operator. A dilation example exhibits identifications of residue kernels beyond scaling and unit-coordinate changes. For nonzero radial residue kernels on bounded inputs, mutual domination is classified by the unit-circle zeros of filter polynomials, counted with multiplicity, with optimal constants given by the $\ell^1$ norms of convolution quotients. We identify the envelope over all normalized bounded cancellative kernels with the best local $L^1$ approximation by constants and prove quantitative convergence of residue envelopes as the resolution increases. Finally, the weights of the finite Fourier transform classify the one-level energy and the associated Carleson functional. This functional is equivalent to the $BMO_2$ seminorm precisely when every nontrivial additive character of the residue field is detected, and the weights determine the optimal comparison constants.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Mohajer

item.title: Boundedness of nonregular bilinear pseudodifferential operators on variable Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we introduce two bilinear, non-regular symbol classes\linebreak $BS\mathcal B^m_\delta(r,\mu,v;N,\lambda)$ and $BS\mathcal F^m_\delta(r,\mu,v;N,\lambda)$, where $m\in\mathbb R$, $0\leq\delta<1$, $0<\mu,v\leq\infty$, $1\leq\lambda\leq2$, $r>n/\mu$, and $N>2n/\lambda$, with $\mu<\infty$ for the latter class. For $\mu\geq1$, $(1-\delta)r\geq n/\mu$, and sufficiently large $N$, we establish boundedness of the associated bilinear pseudodifferential operators on Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with variable smoothness, integrability and summation exponents. To the best of the authors' knowledge, these operator estimates are new even on the classical Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with constant exponents. As an application, we establish the multiplication algebra property for both variable exponent spaces.
item.dc:creator: Tengfei Bai, Jingshi Xu, Jinlai Zhu

item.title: Noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for convolution operators under $L_1$-H\"ormander conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for families of scalar convolution operators acting on operator-valued function spaces. A joint $L_1$-H\"ormander condition, together with a maximal strong type estimate at one exponent $1<r\leq\infty$, suffices. The kernels may be complex-valued and need not have uniformly bounded $L_1$ norms. Under a size condition, the result also yields a weak endpoint estimate for all sharp truncation radii of singular kernels. This resolves, for convolution kernels, the problem mentioned in \cite[Remark~5.5]{parcet09pseudo} and recalled in Parcet's recent survey \cite[Remark~1.3]{Parcet2026ICM}. The proof involves not only a simultaneous dyadic representation of the operators but also a noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates of the resulting dyadic operators. This approach seems entirely new even in the commutative setting. Numerous applications are provided. On the one hand, it yields various maximal inequalities and pointwise convergence results for integrable kernels and dyadic approximations of the identity, monotone $L\log L$ majorants, and Poisson integrals on nilpotent groups and symmetric spaces. On the other hand, via various transference techniques, it implies maximal inequalities for Fourier multipliers, Schur multipliers and double operator integrals, together with bilateral almost uniform convergence of dyadic Fourier summation methods on $L_1$ of group von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Guixiang Hong, Liang Wang, Xumin Wang, Bang Xu

item.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-shrinkers
item.description: arXiv:2610.25831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the global structure of the self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$, without assuming properness or embeddedness. The main tool is a pair of piecewise monotone quantities along the profile curves, in the spirit of Hsiang's analysis of constant mean curvature hypersurfaces. We prove that every such self-shrinker other than the two invariant cylinders intersects both of them transversely, and all of them except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Apart from those of the cylinders, each end is either asymptotic to a cone or meets both cylinders infinitely many times. Consequently, a complete noncompact example is proper if and only if all its ends are asymptotically conical, and this is equivalent to polynomial volume growth, to finite entropy, and to finitely many intersections with the cylinders. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure, and for almost every initial condition the profile curve is either closed or generates a complete nonproper self-shrinker of infinite entropy. We also bound the winding of the profile curve by its number of cylinder crossings and localize its self-intersections.
item.dc:creator: Greg\'orio Silva Neto

item.title: Limits of Besov Norms on Quantum Euclidean Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the Bourgain--Br\'{e}zis--Mironescu (BBM) and Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova (MS) limit formulae to higher-order Besov norms on quantum Euclidean spaces $\R^d_\theta$, a fundamental class of noncompact noncommutative manifolds obtained by deformation quantization of $\R^d$. A central ingredient is a Banach realization of the homogeneous Sobolev endpoint that forms a compatible couple with \(L_p(\R_\theta^d)\), together with the equivalence \[ K\bigl(\x,\varepsilon^k; L_p(\R_\theta^d),\dot W_{p,0}^k(\R_\theta^d)\bigr) \approx \omega_p^k(\x,\varepsilon). \] This framework yields a unified proof of both endpoint formulae through the endpoint continuity of real interpolation scales. The principal new ingredient at the MS endpoint is the sharp large-translation asymptotic \[ \lim_{|h|\to\infty}\|T_h\x-\x\|_p = 2^{1/p}\|\x\|_p, \qquad \x\in L_p(\R_\theta^d),\quad 1\leq p<\infty, \] whose proof combines oscillatory decay of the non-pure terms in the tracial expansion with weighted spectral-measure arguments adapted to the semifinite trace.
item.dc:creator: Qingquan Deng, Guixiang Hong, Ping Li, Yanzhen Long

item.title: The Riemann zeta function at the zeros of real-rooted trigonometric polynomials
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Bryce Kerr, Oleksiy Klurman, Guilherme Vedana

item.title: Muckenhoupt weights for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On the real hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, the classical Muckenhoupt condition does not describe the weights $w$ for which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$. We show that, for $1<p<\infty$, $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$ if and only if $w$ is a local $A_p$ weight and satisfies a two-layer condition, which compares $w$ and its dual weight on two layers of the shadow of a point. We also treat the weak type case, radial weights and the range $p\le1$, and we prove a weighted Herz principle for radial convolution operators.
item.dc:creator: Tapendu Rana

item.title: The Restricted Three-Body Problem as a Perturbed Duffing Equation
item.description: arXiv:2505.07104v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the restricted circular planar three-body problem. We prove that for every negative Jacobi constant of sufficiently large magnitude, the surface of unperturbed parabolic solutions breaks to induce homoclinic tangles for all but at most finitely many mass ratios of primaries. Our approach relies on reformulating the restricted three-body problem as a perturbed Duffing equation by introducing new coordinate transformations. This enables us to capture the order of the singularities involved through a renormalized Duffing Hamiltonian structure, to derive the existence and analytic dependence of the invariant manifolds on the mass ratio of the primaries, and to evaluate the Poincar\'e-Melnikov integral directly through the explicit homoclinic solution of the unperturbed Duffing equation. Compared to existing works, our proof is significantly simpler and more direct. Moreover, the paper is self-contained: we do not rely on McGehee's analysis in \cite{Mc} to justify the applicability of the Poincar\'e-Melnikov method.
item.dc:creator: Rongchang Liu, Qiudong Wang

item.title: Positive Cubature Compression and Optimal Hyperinterpolation Stability on a Conic Surface
item.description: arXiv:2609.36430v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the computational cost and stability of positive cubature and hyperinterpolation on a truncated conic surface with a Jacobi-type weight. A classical quadratic disk-to-cone map is formulated as a measure-preserving $\mathbb Z_2$ quotient. It identifies degree-$m$ conic traces with even disk polynomials of degree at most $2m$ and gives a two-way correspondence between positive degree-$2n$ cone cubature and centrally symmetric positive degree-$(4n+1)$ disk cubature. Consequently, M\"oller's lower bound and the node excess above it transfer exactly, producing compressed non-product cone rules from near-minimal disk formulas. The quotient also transfers reproducing kernels and hyperinterpolation operators. Every positive degree-$2n$ cone rule yields an exact $L^2$ sampling isometry on $\Pi_n(V)$, so the weighted sampling matrix has condition number one, independently of the number and geometry of its nodes. The associated Lebesgue constants satisfy the rule-independent bound $\Lambda_{n,\gamma}^V\ge c_\gamma n^{\gamma+1}$ for every $\gamma>-1$. For nonnegative half-integer $\gamma$, the matching upper bound holds, giving the sharp universal order $\Lambda_{n,\gamma}^V\asymp n^{\gamma+1}$; in particular, $\Lambda_n^V\asymp n$ when $\gamma=0$. Thus node compression preserves exact $L^2$ conditioning and, in this parameter range, optimal-order $L^\infty$ stability. Low-degree near-minimal rules and higher-degree optimized disk schemes illustrate the reduction in sampling cost.
item.dc:creator: Congpei An, Yan Ge

item.title: Assouad Dimensions and Spectra of Graphs of Weierstrass-Type Functions with Rapidly Growing Frequencies
item.description: arXiv:2609.37388v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Assouad dimension, lower dimension, and Assouad spectrum of graphs of the functions \(f(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n\phi(b_nx+\theta_n)\), where \(\phi\) is a nonconstant \(1\)-periodic \(C^2\) function, \(a_n,b_n>0\), \((\theta_n)\) is an arbitrary real sequence, \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n<\infty\), and \(b_{n+1}/b_n\to\infty\). We give sufficient conditions for the graph over every nondegenerate compact interval to have Assouad dimension two or lower dimension one. For \(a_n=b_n^{-\alpha}\), \(0<\alpha<1\), an explicit frequency-gap condition ensures that the Assouad spectrum equals two for \(\alpha\leq\vartheta<1\). Writing \(\beta_*=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\log b_{n+1}/\log b_n\), we show that, if \(\beta_*>(2-\alpha)/\alpha\), the spectrum attains the general upper bound for \(\alpha\)-H\"older graphs whenever \((2-\alpha)/\beta_*\leq\vartheta<\alpha\) and \(\vartheta>0\). When \(\beta_*=\infty\), this determines the complete spectrum. Together with Bara\'nski's formulas, our results yield graphs whose lower, Hausdorff, upper box, and Assouad dimensions are four distinct numbers.
item.dc:creator: Dong-Hong Xiong, Jun Jason Luo

item.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.15981v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Dohmen, Sebastian Scholtes

item.title: Some Cubic and Quartic Inequalities of Four Variables
item.description: arXiv:2202.06508v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H} \subset \mathcal{H}_{n,d} := \mathbb{R}[x_1$,$\ldots$, $x_n]_d$ be a vector space, and $A$ be a compact semialgebraic subset of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{R}}^{n-1}$. We shall study some PSD cones $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}(A$, $\mathcal{H}) := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}$ $\big|$ $f(a) \geq 0$ ($\forall a \in A$)$\big\}$. Our interests are (1) to determine the extremal elements of $\mathcal{P}$, (2) to determine discriminants of $\mathcal{P}$, (3) to describe $\mathcal{P}$ as a union of basic semialgebraic subsets, and (4) to find a nice test set when $\dim \mathcal{H}$ is low. In this article, we present (1), (2), (3) and (4) for $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,4}^{s0})$ and $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}_+^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,4}^{s0})$, where $\mathcal{H}_{n,d}^{s0} := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}_{n,d}$ $\big|$ $f$ is symmetric and $f(1,\ldots,1)=0 \big\}$. We also provide (1) -- (4) for $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}_+^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,3}^{c0})$, where $\mathcal{H}_{n,d}^{c0} := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}_{n,d}$ $\big|$ $f$ is cyclic and $f(1,\ldots,1)=0 \big\}$.
item.dc:creator: Tetsuya Ando

item.title: Asymptotics of Constrained Quantization for Compactly Supported Measures
item.description:
arXiv:2505.10801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study constrained quantization of a compactly supported probability $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^D$ by codebooks in a nonempty closed set $S$. For $0<r\le\infty$, the constrained error $e_{n,r}$ is attained and satisfies $e_{n,r}\downarrow L_r=\|\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)\|_{L^r(P)}$. Set $\Delta_{n,r}=e_{n,r}^r-L_r^r$ for finite $r$. A Borel nearest-point selector $T$ induces $\mu=T_*P$. Writing $q_{n,s}$ for the classical $L^s$ quantization error, we obtain $e_{n,r}-L_r\le2q_{n,r}(\mu)$ and $\Delta_{n,r}\le C_rq_{n,1}(\mu)$ for $1\le r<\infty$, with $C_r$ independent of $n$, and $\Delta_{n,r}\le2^rq_{n,r}(\mu)^r$ for $0<r<1$. Also, $e_{n,\infty}-L_\infty\le2c_n(E)$, where $E$ is the nearest-point image of $\operatorname{supp}P$ and $c_n(E)$ is its covering radius. For $1\le r<\infty$, a weighted power-growth condition with exponent $ eta>0$ on a fixed source set $F$ bounds $\Delta_{n,r}$ below by the classical $ eta$-power quantization cost of $
u_F=T_*(wP|_F)$. If $d
u_F=\widehat w\,d\eta$ for a compactly supported reference probability $\eta$ and $\widehat w\in A_p(\eta)$, $1<p<\infty$, then $\Delta_{n,r}\ge
u_F(\mathbb{R}^D)[\widehat w]_{A_p(\eta)}^{-1}q_{n, eta/p}(\eta)^ eta$. These comparisons yield bounds for the quantization dimensions defined by $e_{n,r}-L_r$ and $\Delta_{n,r}^{1/r}$, with distinct behavior at positive and zero baselines. Convex and uniformly prox-regular constraints supply the growth weights through their projection inequalities. Circle and lifted Cantor distributions give matching quadratic-excess rates, while rectifiable weighted projections give lower Zador estimates.
item.dc:creator: Chenxing Qian

item.title: Universal polar dual pairs]{Universal polar dual pairs of spherical codes found in $E_8$ and the Leech lattice
item.description: arXiv:2512.25037v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify universal polar dual pairs of spherical codes $C$ and $D$ such that for a large class of potential functions $h$ the minima of the discrete $h$-potential of $C$ on the sphere occur at the points of $D$ and vice versa. Moreover, the minimal values of their normalized potentials are equal. These codes arise from the known hierarchies of sharp codes embedded in the even unimodular extremal lattices $E_8$ and $\Lambda_{24}$ (Leech lattice). This embedding allows us to use the lattices' properties to find new universal polar dual pairs. In the process we extensively utilize the interplay between the binary Golay codes and the Leech lattice. As a byproduct of our analysis, we identify a new universally optimal (in the sense of energy) code in the projective space $\mathbb{RP}^{21}$ with $1408$ points (lines). Furthermore, we extend the Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel definition of derived codes from their seminal $1977$ paper and generalize their Theorem 8.2 to show that if a $\tau$-design is enclosed in $k\leq \tau$ parallel hyperplanes, then each derived code is a $(\tau+1-k)$-design in the ambient subspace.
item.dc:creator: S. V. Borodachov, P. G. Boyvalenkov, P. D. Dragnev, D. P. Hardin, E. B. Saff, M. M. Stoyanova

item.title: Galerkin Approximation of the Fractional Sobolev Constant
item.description: arXiv:2605.13347v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish sharp estimates for the discrete optimal constant of the fractional Sobolev inequality in dimension $N\geq 1$, with fractional exponent $s\in (0,\min\{1,N/2\})$. The convergence rates that we establish take place for the Galerkin approximation with piecewise linear elements, when the problem is posed in the unit ball, for which we employ a quasi-uniform and regular mesh. Since the infimum defining the fractional Sobolev constant is not attained on bounded domains, these estimates quantify how far a piecewise affine mesh of size $h$ can resolve the concentration of the optimizers: the discrete minimizers are close to bubbles concentrated at the scale $h^{2(2-s)/(N+4(1-s))}$, and the energy gap is exactly of order $h^{2(2-s)(N-2s)/(N+4(1-s))}$.
item.dc:creator: Andreea Dima, Liviu I. Ignat

item.title: Galois descents of certain multiple polylogarithms
item.description: arXiv:2608.16735v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove some conjectures of K. C. Au concerning the descents of cyclotomic levels in certain sums over multiple polylogarithms. Via answers to a question of Au in some particular cases, we also confirm Broadhurst's conjecture on honorary multiple zeta values at even weights.
item.dc:creator: Yajun Zhou

item.title: Exponential improvements in Rado's covering problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.25288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $B^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball of unit radius. What is the largest constant $f(B^d) \in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $f(B^d)$ of the volume of $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T. Rad\'o in 1928, for axis-parallel squares in the plane; the author was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. The case of Euclidean balls was first considered by R. Rado in 1949. Until last year the best known estimates on $f(B^d)$ for unit balls where very far apart: \[ (1+\epsilon_d) 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2^{-d}, \] where $0<\epsilon_d=o_{d\rightarrow \infty}(1)$. Recently, the authors of this note observed that an exponential improvement on the upper bound follows from the Kabatiansky--Levenshtein spherical code bound, while the lower bound was improved by a linear factor by C.~Xie and G.~Ge (see arxiv:2608.09744). The current best estimates for large $d$ are \[ c \cdot d \cdot 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}, \] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. Here we offer the first exponential improvement of the lower bound in almost 80 years, which narrows the gap to: \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}. \] Our method is constructive and yields a polynomial time algorithm for finding a disjoint sub-collection realizing the estimate. Moreover the same technique gives similar exponentially improved lower bounds for all symmetric convex bodies satisfying a uniform convexity assumption, e.g., $\ell^p$-balls for all $p\in (1,\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Gian Maria Dall'Ara, Adrian Dumitrescu

item.title: The strong reproducing kernel thesis for Hankel operators and the Garsia norm
item.description: arXiv:2609.33242v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a bounded operator $T$ on $\mathcal H$, we say that $T$ obeys the strong reproducing kernel thesis (SRKT) if $\|T\|=\sup_k\|Tk\|$, where $k$ ranges over the normalized reproducing kernels in $\mathcal H$. Two problems are posed. One of these is to determine which Hankel operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ obey the SRKT. The other concerns the geometry of the unit ball of $BMO$ with respect to the Garsia norm.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin M. Dyakonov

item.title: Sharp Truncated Difference Estimates for Nonlocal Nonconvex Functionals Defined by Superlevel Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.04259v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $N\in\mathbb N$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$. In this article, we consider a family $\{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ of nonlocal nonconvex functionals with a real parameter $\gamma$ and establish two truncated difference estimates bounded by these functionals with the sharp range of $\gamma$; that is, for any $\gamma\in(-\infty,-1]$, any $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, any cube $Q\subset\mathbb R^N$, and any measurable function $g:Q\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\int_Q\int_Q\left[\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|-\lambda|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}{\ell(Q)^{1+\gamma/p}}\right]_+^p\,dx\,dy\\ &\quad\lesssim \lambda^p\mathop{\int_Q\int_Q}\limits_{\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|}{|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}>\lambda}\left[\frac{|x-y|}{\ell(Q)}\right]^{\gamma-N}\,dx\,dy=:\frac{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}(g;Q)}{\ell(Q)^{\gamma-N}}, \end{align*} where the implicit positive constant depends only on $N$, $p$, and $\gamma$. For $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, the above estimate holds with the left-most integrand replaced by $\frac{\min\{|g(x)-g(y)|^p,\lambda^p|x-y|^{p+\gamma}\}}{\ell(Q)^{p+\gamma}}$. As applications, these estimates yield related nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities with the sharp range of $\gamma$, and also recover the known $\Gamma$-liminf lower bounds and characterizations of Sobolev and BV spaces in terms of the liminf of the functionals $\{\Phi^\gamma_{\lambda,p}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ for all $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\setminus(-1,0]$. We investigate further applications to compactness and variational problems as well as a new VMO criterion. Inspired by a recent work of R. L. Frank, we develop an elementary approach based on dyadic iteration of truncated differences along line segments, which allows us to treat the aforementioned problems in a unified way.
item.dc:creator: Feng Dai, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Yirui Zhao

item.title: On extremal problems related to the Krzy\.{z} conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23817v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study general extremal problems similar or closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture and establish the structural properties of extremal functions, pointing out some differences with the original Krzy\.z case. We also introduce a family of more specific problems of this kind, interpolating between the Krzy\.z problem and the problem of maximizing the constant term, and show that they are closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture: the conjecture implies the analogous statement for all of them and, conversely, if one of them has the same extremal value as the Krzy\.z problem, then this value is $2/e$. This may represent a new approach to attacking the original problem. Finally, we show that for these problems an extremal function whose Taylor coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ vanish must be the conjectured one; as a special case, we obtain a new proof of a recent result of MacDonald.
item.dc:creator: Sarah May Instanes, Adri\'an Llinares, Dragan Vukoti\'c
